Where symbols share a cell, the voiceless ones come first and the voiced follow the dot. Secondary articulation (ʷ ʲ ˠ ˤ) and length (ː) stay in the cell of the plain sound.

### Vowels

Unrounded vowels come before the dot, rounded after it. Length: long vowels iː ɛː iːᴖ aː əː aːᴖ uːᴖ. Nasality: no nasal vowels.

- **ᴖ** (a second simultaneous voice (syrinx)): iᴖ, aᴖ, uᴖ, əᴖ, iːᴖ, aːᴖ, uːᴖ. Symbol table: second simultaneous source (syrinx two-voice; ᴖ U+1D16).

### Tone, syllables and stress

| tone | IPA | spelling |
| --- | --- | --- |
| low | a˨ | grave à |
| mid | a˧ | unmarked a |
| high | a˦ | acute á |
| rising | a˨˦ | caron ǎ |
| falling | a˦˨ | circumflex â |

The language has 5 phonemic tones, marked on every vowel in the IPA here.
Syllable shapes (share of syllables in the word-shape model): CV 45%, CVC 25%, CCV 11%, CCVC 8%, V 7%, VC 4%. At most 2 consonant(s) before the vowel and 1 after it.
Stress falls on the next-to-last syllable.
Core words average 2.08 syllables (4.3 sounds); 17% of words share their form with another word.

### Allophony

This output records no allophones (the engine stores sounds as phonemes only).

## Orthography

The house romanization in two registers: the full spelling (workbench, one letter or digraph per sound, tone marks) and the book spelling (lossy: no tone, plain vowels, at most one diacritic letter a word).

**Consonants:** n ‹n› · ȵ ‹ň› · ɳ ‹ṇ› · ɲ ‹ny› · ŋ ‹ng› · p ‹p› · t ‹t› · d ‹d› · ʈ ‹ṭ› · k ‹k› · ɡ ‹g› · ʔ ‹'› · dʒ ‹j› · s ‹s› · ʂ ‹ṣ› · f ‹f› · x ‹kh› · ħ ‹ḥ› · ʕ ‹ʿ› · h ‹h› · ɦ ‹hh› · ʋ ‹v› · ɹ ‹ř› ‹r› · j ‹y› · w ‹w› · l ‹l› · ɫ ‹ll› · r ‹rr› · ɾ ‹r›

**Vowels:** i ‹i› · iᴖ ‹iwh› · iː ‹ii› · iːᴖ ‹iiwh› · ɯ ‹eu› · uᴖ ‹uwh› · uːᴖ ‹uuwh› · e ‹e› · ə ‹ë› ‹e› · əᴖ ‹ewh› · əː ‹ëë› ‹ee› · ɛ ‹è› ‹e› · ɛː ‹èe› ‹ee› · a ‹a› · aᴖ ‹awh› · aː ‹aa› · aːᴖ ‹aawh›

Tones are written over the vowel: low grave à, mid unmarked a, high acute á, rising caron ǎ, falling circumflex â (Yoruba-style).

Where two spellings are given the second is the book spelling.

## Grammar

Basic word order is SOV; it has postpositions. In the noun phrase: possessor before the possessed; adjective order varies; demonstrative before the noun; noun before the numeral; noun before the relative clause. Overall it is head-final.
It has no definite article, no indefinite article, a rich case system, split alignment (ergative in some contexts, accusative in others), singular and plural, gender by animacy.
Verbs mark perfective; there are no evidentials. Negation uses a negator before the verb; yes/no questions use a final question particle. Verbs do not agree with their arguments.
Other features: pronouns can be dropped; an inclusive/exclusive 'we' distinction; serial verbs; a copula; a bound causative; no passive; question words moved to the front; a decimal counting base.
Note on the data: the typology features and the live markers disagree here (indefinite article is 'none' but an indefinite marker is live (INDEF); future is 'none' but a future marker is live (FUT); progressive is 'none' but a progressive marker is live (PROG)). Both are shown as recorded.
Measured morphology: 14 live grammatical markers, mean bondedness 1.7 (0 free word … 3 fused), 52 paradigm cells, 16 of them with allomorphy.
